The inverse branch h_w(y)=(2^A y-B_w)/3^|w| is an affine homeomorphism O_2->U_w, child balls are nested and disjoint, and U_w is the disjoint union of its one terminated boundary point h_w(-1/3) and all child balls U_wa.

statement: The positive itinerary image Sigma_C^+ is countable, dense, proper, and nonclosed in the full exponent shift because every finite word has infinitely many positive sources. It is forward-shift stable but not shift-surjective: sigma(Sigma_C^+)=epsilon_2({y positive odd:3 does not divide y}) is a strict subset, since positive predecessors exist exactly for targets not divisible by three.

statement: For an infinite exponent word, its canonical positive prefix representatives satisfy r_(n+1)=r_n+k_n 2^(A_n+1), 0<=k_n<2^(a_(n+1)), and hence form a nondecreasing integer sequence. The word comes from a positive odd integer exactly when these representatives are bounded, equivalently eventually constant, and the eventual constant is the unique source. The rooted tree with vertices (w,A(w)+1,r_w) has full-shift end space and selects positive ends by this exact stabilization criterion.

statement: For phi(a)=log 3-a_1 log 2 on the full countable shift, the n-block partition sum is finite exactly for beta>0 and then equals (((3/2)^beta)/(1-2^(-beta)))^n, with pressure beta log(3/2)-log(1-2^(-beta)) and exact Bernoulli weights (1-2^(-beta))2^(-beta(a-1)). At beta<=0 the one-symbol sum diverges. The full shift is the TMS of the complete countable graph, is topologically mixing and BIP, and beta phi is one-cylinder locally constant with zero higher variations and finite supremum for beta>0. For every beta>0 the countable positive itinerary image has measure zero under this full-shift Gibbs law.

statement: The path bidegree deg(p)=(ell(p),A(p)-ell(p)) is a functor from the odd path category to the one-object additive monoid category N_0^2. With Q=R_{>=0}^2, the translated-quadrant map j(r,s)=(r,s)+Q injects this monoid into the multiplicative monoid of Connes-Consani Conv(Z^2) under Minkowski sum. Over (r,s), r>=1, the word component of the degree fibre has binomial(r+s-1,r-1) exponent compositions, each with its exact infinite arithmetic source fibre; over (0,0) every object identity occurs, and every fibre over (0,s) with s>0 is empty.

statement: For a nonzero commutative semiring K, the K-linear degree map from the finite-support category semialgebra K[E_C] to K[N_0^2] is not multiplicative: distinct object identities multiply to zero but both map to the target unit. Separately, on the path semigroup with absorbing zero, the zero-preserving set map theta(0)=empty and theta(p)=j(deg p) is multiplicative on composable pairs but not globally: theta(1_x1_y)=empty for x!=y whereas theta(1_x)theta(1_y)=Q+_Mink Q=Q. No coefficient-semiring map into Conv(Z^2) is asserted. The typed matrix representation retaining object units is the algebraic repair.
nonclaims: Failure of these exact object-erasing formulas does not rule out typed tropical representations.
The translated-quadrant statement is a semigroup-with-zero obstruction, not an untyped composition of a monomial algebra map with j.

statement: Connes and Consani construct the arithmetic-site tensor square, its reduction via Newton polygons in Conv(Z x Z), and Frobenius maps and correspondences. Their composition theorem has three exact cases: if lambda lambda' is irrational, Psi(lambda) composed with Psi(lambda') equals Psi(lambda lambda'); if both parameters are positive rational, the same equality holds; if both are irrational and their product is positive rational, the composition is id_epsilon composed with Psi(lambda lambda'). The source also distinguishes diagonal Frobenius from a power map and records noncancellativity before reduction.

statement: Bhatt and Lurie define WCart_X for bounded p-adic formal schemes, make it functorial in formal-scheme maps, identify the Spf(Z_p) base case by finality, and treat Witt Frobenius as a separate endomorphism. statement: Every continuous unital endomorphism of Z_3 is the identity, so g_a(x)=(3x+1)/2^a is not an endomorphism of Spf(Z_3), already because g_a(0)=2^(-a) is nonzero. The coordinate substitution T->(3T+1)/2^a does define an endomorphism of the formal affine line Spf(Z_3<T>); on Z_3-points it is injective with image 2^(-a)+3Z_3 and the displayed inverse. For every a,k>=1 and every residue b mod 3^k, CRT constructs positive odd points in the same 3-adic ball with valuations a and a+1. Thus the integer a-stratum and its complement meet every finite 3-adic residue ball, and no clopen subset of Z_3 cuts out that stratum on the positive odd integers.
nonclaims: No WCart(g_a) on the formal point is admitted.
The formal-affine-line endomorphism does not assemble the Collatz piecewise map or supply its 2-adic exponent selector.
The CRT theorem rules out a clopen finite-level 3-adic selector on positive odds; it does not assert that every richer mixed-adic construction is impossible.
No prismatic or crystalline Collatz theorem follows.

statement: For W the Witt vectors of a perfect field of characteristic p and a primitive pth root zeta, Gros, Le Stum, and Quiros work over the one-variable ring W[[q-1]]. Their Theorem 7.5 uses complete modules with Delta-hyperstratification, while Theorem 7.12 identifies the stated finite-free weakly nilpotent Delta-modules and prismatic vector bundles. Their later sections treat de Rham, Hodge-Tate, Frobenius, crystalline-representation, and Wach-module comparisons at their printed scopes.

statement: Sarig's 1999 article defines the countable-shift Gurevich-pressure and recurrence/Ruelle-Perron-Frobenius framework. Its Theorem 8, for a topologically mixing shift and a locally Holder potential of finite Gurevich pressure, says that a Gibbs measure exists exactly when the potential is positive recurrent, its RPF eigenfunction is uniformly bounded above and below, and condition (13) holds; condition (13) is the one-sided big-images condition, not BIP. In that case the Gibbs measure is h nu and its pressure parameter equals the Gurevich pressure. His 2003 theorem treats a topologically mixing countable Markov shift with summable variations, finite first variation, and finite Gurevich pressure, and characterizes existence of an invariant Gibbs measure by BIP at that scope. His distinct 2015 overview restates the pressure, recurrence, variational, equilibrium, Gibbs, and BIP boundaries at its separately cited theorem locators.

statement: For a positive exponent word w=(a_1,...,a_n), with A_k=sum_(j<=k)a_j, the raw arctangent programme defines theta_k=arctan(3^(k-1)/2^A_k), z_k=2^A_k+i3^(k-1), u_k=z_k/conj(z_k), and Rel_pi(w)={m in Z^n:sum m_k theta_k in pi Q}. Chronologically, its corrected endpoint is the exact multiplicative torsion test product u_k^(m_k) in mu_4, not an additive unit equation or a universal nonvanishing theorem.
nonclaims: The raw chronology does not prove that the relation lattice is zero.
No zeta, Heegner, modular, CM, operator, or endpoint implication is admitted from exploratory rhetoric.

statement: Conway, Radin, and Sadun's d=1 Stormer reconstruction uses unique factorization in Z[i], one oriented Gaussian prime above each split rational prime, and pi/4 to give exact fixed-instance coordinates and rational independence for rational-tangent angles at their stated scope.

statement: Gasull, Luca, and Varona classify their stated two-term nonzero-right-hand-side Machin formulas with 2-integer arguments; their Theorem 1 contains arctan(1/2)+(1/2)arctan(3/4)=pi/4, and their Section 2 supplies the corresponding Gaussian root-of-unity reformulation.

statement: For every fixed positive exponent word w, the homomorphism Gamma_bar_w:Z^n->U_1(Q(i))/mu_4 followed by the oriented split-prime valuation isomorphism nu_G gives the exact signed-valuation map E_w. Its kernel is Rel_pi(w); each nonempty fibre is one coset of Rel_pi(w), every point outside im(E_w) has empty fibre, and Z^n/Rel_pi(w)->im(E_w) has the displayed inverse on cosets. Reorienting one split prime negates only that coordinate.
source_locators: Conway-Radin-Sadun source lines 251-306; independent exact morphism reconstruction
nonclaims: Fixed-word decidability after exact factorization is not a uniform rank classification.

statement: For every nonempty positive exponent word w, sum_k arctan(3^(k-1)/2^A_k) is not in pi Q, equivalently the all-ones coefficient vector is not in Rel_pi(w). The exact proof multiplies z_k=2^A_k+i3^(k-1): modulo 3 both real and imaginary parts are nonzero, and modulo 2 they have opposite parity, excluding all four values of Z/conj(Z) in mu_4.

nonclaims: The theorem concerns only the coefficient vector (1,...,1), not all integer relations.
It proves no Collatz orbit endpoint.

Therefore every word with n<=15 and A_n<=60 has relation lattice Z(2,1,0,...,0) exactly when its first two exponents are (1,1), and zero otherwise.

statement: Collatz-Machin rigidity conjecture: for every nonempty positive exponent word w=(a_1,...,a_n), Rel_pi(w)=Z(2,1,0,...,0) when n>=2 and (a_1,a_2)=(1,1), and Rel_pi(w)={0} otherwise.

nonclaims: The conjecture is not a theorem outside the certified grid.

statement: The unshortened positive-integer map U, shortened integer/2-adic map T, and Crandall odd first-return map C_Cr have distinct source conventions and clocks.
nonclaims: The maps are not normalized into one fixed-time system.

statement: For positive odd x, C_Cr(x)=T^{e(x)}(x)=U^{e(x)+1}(x), with the displayed intermediate values and first-return minimality.
nonclaims: This is variable-time, not a fixed-iterate conjugacy.

statement: Positive run-length sequences are bijective with binary sequences beginning in one and containing infinitely many ones; the inverse is consecutive one-position gaps.
The shortened parity code of a positive odd orbit factors as P=B o E; accelerated shift is variable-time shortened shift; E is injective but no surjectivity onto all run sequences is asserted.
nonclaims: Arbitrary run sequences are not claimed to arise from positive integers.

statement: A length-L chronological branch word with m ones at v_r has affine value (3^m z + sum_r 3^{m-r-1}2^{v_r})/2^L.
nonclaims: The formal word is an actual iterate only after itinerary correctness.

statement: Bohm-Sontacchi printed Proposition 4 is false under its unrestricted iterate quantifiers; x=0, m=1, n_0=n_1=1 gives formal value 1/4 but T^3(0)=0.
nonclaims: The formal affine-composition identity is not contradicted.

statement: Bohm-Sontacchi Proposition 5 omits the visible final inequality v_(m-1)<v_m=n; the literal omission admits x=-2 at m=n=1, while the run construction restores the strict inequality.
Every 2-adically integral formal fixed-return fraction has the prescribed actual T itinerary; conversely every T return has that fraction; exact period divides the displayed return length.
nonclaims: A return length is not automatically a least period.

statement: The Bernstein-Lagarias chronological parity encoder Q_3 is a 2-adic isometric bijection with inverse Phi_3 and Q_3 o T=S o Q_3.
nonclaims: Q_3 and Phi_3 have inverse orientations and are not interchangeable names.

statement: Crandall Eq. (7.3) is the shortened parity-word return equation under cumulative first-return positions A_j.
nonclaims: The equation characterizes returns and does not exclude nontrivial cycles.

statement: The inverse parity image of a purely periodic chronological word is exactly the Bohm-Sontacchi fixed-return fraction, and its exact T-period equals the least shift period of the infinite word.
Laarhoven-de Weger's Phi is the chronological parity encoder Q_3 in Bernstein-Lagarias orientation, not Bernstein-Lagarias Phi_3=Q_3^{-1}.
nonclaims: The inverse notation difference is not a mathematical disconnection.

statement: For every f on positive integers with f(N) tending to infinity, U_min(N)<f(N) for logarithmic-density-one N.
nonclaims: Not natural density.
Not convergence to one.
Not a universal constant bound.

statement: Matthews reserves d(T) for the least affine modulus and defines relatively-prime type there; on any retained d>=2 the branch formula T(x)=(m_i x-r_i)/d extends uniquely and continuously from Z to Z_d, while the presentation-level condition gcd(m_i,d)=1 for every branch forces d=d(T) and hence is exactly the source's relatively-prime type.
nonclaims: The displayed presentation modulus is not silently identified with the least affine modulus d(T); their equality is used only after it is proved from the unit condition.

statement: For a relatively-prime Matthews map, each length-alpha itinerary cylinder is exactly the residue class b_alpha+d^alpha Z_d, where b_alpha is the truncated inverse series; finite itinerary encoders are permutations modulo d^alpha.
nonclaims: Arbitrary unrelated moduli m require the separate gcd(m_i,m) predecessor condition.

statement: For every relatively-prime Matthews map, the chronological residue-itinerary encoder It_T:Z_d->Z_d is an isometric homeomorphism with explicit inverse sum_j r_(i_j)d^j/(m_(i_0)...m_(i_j)) and conjugates the d-adic extension to the full digit shift.
nonclaims: No novelty claim is made.
The encoder is not asserted to be additive or a ring homomorphism.
The conjugacy does not identify the positive-integer subset with a solved shift-invariant subset.

statement: If gcd(m_i,d)>1 on a branch, only d/gcd(m_i,d) second digits can follow i and every attainable digit has gcd(m_i,d) lifts; the canonical itinerary encoder misses two-digit cylinders and is not a full-shift bijection.
nonclaims: This is an obstruction to the canonical itinerary encoder, not a categorical nonexistence theorem for every conceivable conjugacy.

statement: For the shortened 3x+1 map, the generalized itinerary encoder specializes pointwise to Bernstein-Lagarias Q_3 and Laarhoven-de Weger's Phi orientation; it supplies an explicit representative of the Matthews C_T orientation, while the Matthews theorem alone does not normalize C_T pointwise.
nonclaims: A shared conjugacy equation alone does not identify two unnamed or unnormalized conjugacies pointwise.

statement: An rcwa map f:Z->Z is affine on residue classes modulo a presentation modulus; Kohl's reduced least-modulus coefficient list has primitive triples with positive denominators, while Algorithm 2.2 also accepts unreduced nonminimal input presentations.
nonclaims: The later rcwa group algorithms are not included in this targeted claim.

statement: At every retained d>=2, Matthews data and pairs consisting of d plus a reduced rcwa list at d with nonzero slopes correspond exactly: (m_i,r_i) maps to the reduction of (m_i,-r_i,d), the inverse is m_i=a_i d/c_i and r_i=-b_i d/c_i, and both round trips are literal after the displayed reduction step. Forgetting d through modulus minimization can lose refinement data; branchwise reduction at retained d does not.
nonclaims: No modulus minimization or coefficient normalization is performed by the edition.
Under the presentation-level unit condition d is least and Kohl Div(T)=d, so for d>=2 Matthews relatively-prime type excludes Kohl integrality; neither condition is integer-map bijectivity.

statement: Kohl Remark 1.2's printed statistic (1/q) sum_i c_i/a_i is false for signed slopes: the same paper's rcwa permutation f(n)=-n has reduced modulus-one triple (-1,0,1), giving -1 rather than the asserted bijective value 1; zero slopes also make the printed expression undefined.
nonclaims: The positive-slope Collatz calculation in the source is unchanged.

statement: For a reduced rcwa list at modulus q, D(f)=(1/q) sum_(a_i nonzero) c_i/|a_i| is at most 1 for injections, at least 1 for surjections, and equal to 1 for bijections; zero-slope branch images have density zero.
nonclaims: This integer-image statistic does not imply d-adic conjugacy or a positive-integer orbit endpoint.

statement: Urata's full map phi:Z_2\{0,-1/3}->Z_2^times has separate odd and even normalization branches; on odd units its inverse fibre over y is exactly {(2^p y-1)/3:p>=1}, with p equal to v_2(3x+1).
nonclaims: The invariance phi(2x+1/3)=phi(x) is not itself a conjugacy.
The even-input branch is not identified with the odd first-return dynamics.

statement: For an actual accelerated odd-unit orbit, 2^(S_n)x_n=C_n+3^n x_0; common first n exponents determine a 2-adic prefix and a complete exponent sequence determines at most one surviving input.
nonclaims: The source's C notation is retained through an explicitly typed reindexing.

statement: Urata Proposition 4 compares approximants sharing only the first m exponents using the later sum S_n; for p_1=1,p_2=3, x_1=1/3 and x_2=11/9 have distance 2^-3, contradicting the printed S_2=4 bound 2^-4.
nonclaims: This does not refute Proposition 4's realization theorem.
The official C formula is not replaced by the later derivative's correction commentary.

statement: Every positive exponent sequence p has the unique surviving odd-unit realization -sum_(j>=1) 2^(S_(j-1))/3^j; suffixes satisfy 3x_k+1=2^(p_(k+1))x_(k+1), proving exact valuations, survival and Urata Proposition 4 without the defective Cauchy bound.
nonclaims: No novelty claim is made.
The realization domain is the 2-adic survivor X, not positive odd integers.

statement: On X=Z_2^times minus the accelerated preimage tree of -1/3, the exponent encoder E_U is a homeomorphism onto (Z_{>=1})^N_0 with the explicit inverse series and conjugates phi to the one-sided countable full shift.
nonclaims: Urata proves uniqueness and existence but does not state the full-shift conjugacy or explicit inverse in this form.
This is variable-time accelerated dynamics.

statement: For exponent word w=(p_1,...,p_n), F_w(U_2)=F_w(1)+2^(S_n+1)Z_2 and normalized odd-unit Haar mass is 2^-S_n; after deleting the countable singular tree, E_U transports Haar measure to the Bernoulli law Pr(p_j=k)=2^-k and the system is strongly mixing.
nonclaims: The variable modulus is 2^(S_n+1), not 2^n.
This is not an ordinary-integer density theorem.

statement: For x in the odd 2-adic survivor, phi^j(x)=T^(S_j)(x) and its shortened chronological parity word is B(E_U(x)); the survivor corresponds exactly to binary sequences beginning in one and containing infinitely many ones.
nonclaims: The positive-integer exponent encoder E remains only injective.
Presentations by binary parity and positive run lengths are connected by the proved map B and are not normalized into the same clock.

statement: A surviving accelerated orbit returns after n steps iff (2^(S_n)-3^n)x=C_n iff its exponent sequence is n-periodic; the least accelerated period equals the least exponent-shift period, while the resulting rational point need not be integral.
nonclaims: Return after a displayed n does not assert least period n.
Urata leaves the integrality question open.
The generalized rational eventual-periodicity paragraph is conjectural.

statement: Siegel's v3 pre-Hydra data consist of a global field K, a proper nonzero ideal Lambda of O_K, and invertible affine F-linear branches H_j(z)=r_j(z)+c_j indexed by O_K/Lambda; the piecewise evaluator chooses the branch indexed by the input coset.
nonclaims: The opening finite Z-basis assertion applies to number fields, not the paper's function-field scope.
An arbitrary F-linear branch need not be scalar or bounded at every place.
The literal global-integrality clause is not used without the separately recorded repair.

statement: For a proper ideal with at least two cosets, source Definition 5.3's demand that every branch map every global integer to a global integer contradicts Definition 5.4's demand that branch j be integer-valued exactly on j+Lambda; the consistent predicates are selected-branch admissibility, exact integrality among global integers, and a separately stronger completion-level inverse-integrality condition.
nonclaims: The repaired predicates are editorial and independently proved, not silently attributed to the source.
Global exact integrality does not imply the completion-level inverse-image identity needed for backward branch correctness.

statement: At retained D, scalar selected-branch-admissible Hydras on Z correspond exactly to Matthews presentations H_i(n)=(m_i n-s_i)/D with s_i congruent to i*m_i modulo D; branch exact-integrality holds exactly when gcd(m_i,D)=1, with no modulus minimization.

The morphism applies only to scalar branches over Q and does not identify a general F-linear Hydra with an rcwa map.
The retained modulus is part of the presentation and is not normalized away.

statement: Siegel Proposition 4.2 is false with uniform discreteness alone: in Q((t)) with the t-adic norm, Y=Z and T(n)=n+1 give a uniformly separated bounded nonpreperiodic orbit; replacing the hypothesis by bounded finiteness makes the source proof valid.
nonclaims: Bounded escape in the full Minkowski embedding does not imply divergence under every individual archimedean absolute value.
The correction does not certify the Correspondence Principle.

statement: For least-significant-digit-first word w=(j_1,...,j_N), H_w=H_(j_1) o ... o H_(j_N), M_(i wedge j)=M_i o M_j, and X_(i wedge j)=M_i(X_j)+X_i; the rightmost branch acts first and the finite numen is the exact affine translation cocycle.
nonclaims: This is an address-to-affine-map construction, not an orbit-itinerary map.

nonclaims: Any use of M_H(n) requires a canonical digit word and retained length.
No p-adic extension or conjugacy follows from this finite quotient.

statement: Functions f:N_0->K satisfying f(pn+j)=r_j(f(n))+c_j correspond exactly to initial values a with (I-r_0)a=c_0; when I-r_0 is invertible the solution is unique and its canonical N-digit formula is P_N(a)+sum_(m<N)P_m(c_(d_m)).

statement: For m>=1 and A>=m, with g=gcd(m,A), the number of primitive pointed exponent words is W(m,A)=sum_(d|g)mu(d)binom(A/d-1,m/d-1).
